chapter: Early New Orleans bands and records
title: Playing left-handed
summary: Sharkey is naturally left-handed and plays cornet that way; left-handed bass and guitar players.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah. I was going to ask you, I just happen to think, keep changing the subject about you're left handed I guess.
Well I'm naturally left handed Bill. And naturally when I picked up the cornet I had a tendency to play it left handed. Yeah. And I... Did it bother you any? No real handicap then?
In other words, a left handed person has the same amount of ability with his left hand as
a right hand man has. Of course the horn is made sort of to hold easier the other way around the valve. Yeah. It doesn't bother you.
No, no. Naturally I have to put my hand over the bell of the instrument. Yeah.
No, because I don't hold the horn straight. I slant the horn.
You're used to it now anyway.
Yeah. Oh, no trouble at all.

Not very many people played the bass or those, I noticed when you were showing how Chink or different people would play the bass you'd do it left handed too. I guess Sherwood's the only left handed bass player I know.
Yeah. Sherwood and, wait they have another one. Is there another one there? I think there's another fella plays with Doth Angels.
I don't know his name but he plays left handed too. Maybe I've seen him in and forgot about it.
Yeah, he played left handed. Yeah.
It's a little more trouble for them. They have to change the stringing of the bass and the round, change the bridge and sound post and all that. Well I don't think it's much trouble, no.

No. And the guitar players all they've got to do is change the strings. Yeah, change the strings and it's all ready to go. Because you have the same technique in, well if I was to play guitar I'd have the same technique that you have in your left hand I'd have it in my right hand.
